name: Ryan R. Posh
title: Assistant Professor of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering
department: Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering; R.E.A.L. Limbs Lab
fitReason: New 2026 Assistant Professor with direct relevance to learned assistive-device control. Full recent research validates RL-selected impedance controllers on an actual powered knee/ankle prosthesis; the demonstrated apparatus was at his prior Michigan host. Current Ohio State visitor capacity is unknown.

physicalEvidence.summary: Full July 2026 methods use TD3 to personalize continuous phase-dependent knee/ankle impedance parameters in a replay-constrained MuJoCo model. Three participants then walked on the actual powered prosthesis at 0.8 m/s. The full protocol evaluates 25 simulation-selected candidates with frozen actor parameters before human-in-the-loop TD3 refinement. Neural RL tunes the impedance controller; it is not an end-to-end neural torque policy. All authors and the human-subject approval belong to Michigan, before his Ohio State move. This is genuine recent physical validation with prior-host apparatus, not verified Ohio State equipment.

fitReason: Spatial-AI and embodied-perception backup with a separate live master’s research-intern inquiry. The documented 2024 Assistant Professor appointment and current 3D human-motion methods fit the new-AP priority; no robot-control deployment is claimed.

physicalEvidence.summary: Full March 2026 BioCoach fuses visual features and inferred 3D skeletal kinematics with exercise-specific joint selection and structured biomechanical context. Training updates selection/cross-attention modules while freezing a 3D CNN and LLaMA-2-7B. Evaluation uses reannotated exercise videos and generated-feedback metrics. It does not actuate a robot or establish clinical efficacy. Force/muscle reasoning and broader sensing are future directions, not completed physical deployment.
